comment: What must not silently disappear from release. `prose` names guardrails no code enforces; `split` declares which half of the skill is deterministic; `baseline` names the offline, $0 checks pinned against a real run.

prose.pattern: A release is done only when the tag is read back from the re
prose.rationale: The one rule. Every intermediate signal in this path can succeed while no tag is cut — a dispatch exits 0 for a run that later fails, a promotion can merge while the release job errors, and _release.yml no-ops on an existing tag so a 'successful' retry can correct nothing. Lose this line and the skill starts reporting releases that did not happen.

prose.pattern: [Nn]ever run `cut` without naming the `collateral` list to the user first
prose.rationale: A dev -> main promotion is a single merge of all of dev and cannot be made selective, so every other bumped-but-untagged component has its bump moved to main alongside the one being released. Until 2026-08-02 that also RELEASED them — the release jobs ran on push, so a merge tagged and npm-published everything within seconds, irreversibly. They are now workflow_dispatch-only and cut dispatches exactly one component, so the blast radius is gone; the disclosure stays because the user should still know what their promotion moves and which components are now one dispatch from a release nobody asked for.

prose.pattern: It is raw material, not the entry
prose.rationale: changelog-draft emits grouped commit subjects, which say what was typed rather than what changed for a reader or what breaks. Shipping the draft verbatim produces release notes that look complete and inform nobody. The prose is the model's job; deleting this line is how it silently stops being done.

prose.pattern: API-stability promise, and no commit message is entitled to make it
prose.rationale: Conventional-commit tooling maps a breaking change to a major bump, which for an 0.x component means silently declaring 1.0.0. shipflow caps it at minor and reports capped: true; this line is what makes the agent surface the cap rather than quietly accept it.

prose.pattern: will usually return `done: false`, and that is not an error
prose.rationale: cut is bounded and resumable because the full path outlasts a single call. Without this line an agent reads the first `done: false` as a failure and either reports the release as broken or starts working around it by hand with gh — abandoning every guard that makes the flow safe.

prose.pattern: [Nn]ever ask about anything in that table
prose.rationale: The whole preflight table is fact: the version on main, the last tag, the unreleased commit count, the blockers. Asking the user to confirm any of it is the UX failure that makes a skill feel like a form, and it is the reason this skill can get to a decision in two questions.

prose.pattern: Never claim a result you did not observe
prose.rationale: Honesty about what was verified is the whole house contract. A skill that reports success it did not witness is worse than one that reports nothing.

prose.pattern: it never reimplements a single thing shipflow does
prose.rationale: Every mutating step belongs to shipflow; this skill resolves the binary, gates its version, and shapes its output. The moment release.js grows its own version reading or PR opening, the two drift and a user gets different behaviour depending on which one they invoked — the exact failure shipflow's own SKILL.md warns about for CI scaffolding.

deterministic.step: read every component's release state, blockers and collateral
group the commits since the last tag into changelog sections
write the version into every version file and splice the CHANGELOG
drive the branch to a tag and read the tag back from the remote

nondeterministic.step: which bump this release actually is
nondeterministic.why: commit types are a suggestion, not a decision — only a person knows whether a refactor broke someone, and whether an 0.x component is ready to claim 1.0.0
grouped commit subjects are raw material; a release note explains why a change was made and what breaks, which no commit message reliably records

nondeterministic.step: whether the collateral releases are acceptable
nondeterministic.why: a promotion is atomic, so releasing one component releases every other bumped one — only the user can say whether shipping those today is fine

_baseline_comment: Pinned against real runs of this skill against this repo, never synthetic fixtures. Offline and $0 by construction: no network, no model, so CI cannot spend and cannot flake. What is frozen is the INPUT (real release-status output) and the rendered draft; what tracks live state is asserted with floors instead, so a release does not make the fixtures stale.

baseline.update_command: node evals/baseline/update.mjs && node scripts/release.js changelog-draft --from evals/baseline --out evals/baseline
baseline.rationale: The frozen run, pinned by MANIFEST.json: the recorded command is re-run into a fresh temp directory and byte-compared, so the eval fails when BEHAVIOUR changes rather than merely when someone edits a fixture. Byte-exactness is correct here and not elsewhere in this set — the rendered draft IS the artifact the author edits, so one dropped bullet is a lost change. The command is offline by construction (it re-renders from frozen release-status output rather than calling shipflow), which is what keeps a CI gate from costing money or flaking.

The real `release-status` outputs the golden renders from, plus the assertion that they still span the three shapes the grouper behaves differently on: many commits across 3+ types, exactly one, and exactly zero. (Not the state machine too, despite what this rationale used to claim — all three fixtures are `state: "clean"`, and no test here asserts any `state` value; shipflow's own `tests/release.test.mjs` is what pins the state machine, including the `devAhead` / `dev-ahead-of-main` shapes from issue #173.) Without this, a refresh that collapsed every fixture to 'no commits' would leave the byte-comparison above passing over nothing — the fixture set would still exist and would still check anything.

The known-bad half, without which the goldens above would keep passing while the checker rotted. Three refusals are asserted directly: changelog-draft on a component with nothing to release exits non-zero rather than emitting an empty entry; cut without --expect-status-hash exits non-zero rather than proceeding to an irreversible tag; and the grouper places a commit of an unknown or non-conventional type in Uncategorised rather than dropping it — a drop produces a plausible, complete-looking entry, which is the failure nobody would ever notice.

Every skill in the monorepo, asserted with a floor rather than equality. Two ways this skill can go quietly blind: the component resolver matching nothing and reporting every component healthy over an empty set, and a newly-shipped skill never being added to release.components so preflight reports on 12 of 13 while looking complete. Both are asserted — every declared component must resolve to a real CHANGELOG, a real version file and a real caller workflow, and every directory under skills/ must be declared.
